: It's up to you if you want to keep my changes or revert back.  You're the admin so it's your site ''':P'''.  Whitespace is easily fixed.  With the HTML table, we can create two columns, and align the text within those columns.  Design-wise, it's cleaner.<br><br>Here's a comparison (scroll down for the HTML table version):<br>- [[User:Sinnic|Sinnic]] 02:18, 26 Dec 2005 (UTC)

:: You can have multiple columns and align text within them just fine without using HTML; I do not understand why you think it is cleaner design-wise.  Near as I can tell wiki syntax is much simpler to work with... --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 02:42, 26 Dec 2005 (UTC)

::: I agree that wiki syntax is much easier to work with.  But when I tried to make '''list=''' a wiki table, it broke the [[Template:Infobox chapters]] code (creating a new row makes it think I'm trying to pass a new value).  I could've wrote the wiki table on one long line without any carriage returns, but that would kind of defeat the purpose...  It may be a little more work to create these Infobox Chapters templates (work I'm will to take on myself), but it only needs to be done once.<br>The columns are for readability.  I find it way easier to find a chapter number or name with a column dedicated to each.  It also looks very clean.  But if you want a better reason, it looks closer to the Table of Contents pages in the actual Wheel of Time books ''':P'''
